title: Maximum Element in Array
statement:
You are given an array of `n` integers. Print the largest value stored in the array.

The array may contain negative numbers and repeated values. If the largest value appears several times, print it once.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum element of the array.

examples.explanation: The values are 3, -2, 9, 4 and 9. The largest is 9 (it appears twice, but we print it once).
All values are negative, so the maximum is the one closest to zero, which is -1.
A single-element array: that element is the maximum.

hints: Every element has to be looked at at least once, so a single pass is the best you can hope for.
Keep a variable holding the largest value seen so far and update it whenever you meet a bigger element.
Initialise that variable with the first element, not with 0: the array can contain only negative numbers.
